newsitem.title: LATVIA: KAIJA SEES SALES, PROFIT 10-15 PCT UP IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: KAIJA SEES SALES, PROFIT 10-15 PCT UP IN 1997.

text.p: Kaija fish cannery transferred to the Riga bourse official list today, increasing the number of official stocks to five, said on Tuesday it saw a 10 to 15 percent growth of both sales and profit in 1997.
"If our sales will grow by 10 to 15 percent as planned, our aim is to increase our profit for a percentage not smaller than that," Gunar Vasks, member of the board, told a news conference.
The company plans to produce 4,717 tonnes during the first six months of 1997 against 8,411 tonnes in the whole of 1996.
The company earlier reported a 1996 profit of 639,843 on net turnover of 11,4 million lats and has forecast a 1997 profit of 1.1 million lats.

Kaija does not expect a significant growth of sales on the local market as consumption shows a tendency to fall due to low purchasing power and more than 80 local fish processors competing on the market.
"It is the lower quality and cheaper produce which dominates at the moment," Vasks said.
